correctness.rationale: Reconstructed h_k-g_k=z/(1-z)^2 and h_k integral in w=1-z with epsilon=1-k. The rescaling epsilon^3 h_k(1-epsilon y) has derivative -(2-epsilon y)/(y^3(1+(1-epsilon)y)); its positive-real integration constant converges to H(y)=y^-2-2/y+2log(1+1/y), whose derivative is -2/[y^3(1+y)]. Since g_k=h_k-Koebe, epsilon^3F_k -> 2Re H, not H alone. On the disk, |F_k(z)|<=C/(d^2(epsilon+d)), d=|1-z|, from straight-segment integration. Polar scaling r=1-epsilon x, theta=epsilon t gives majorant x^beta/[(x+|t|)^(2q)(1+x+|t|)^q]; integrable near origin exactly when 2q<beta+2, and at infinity when 3q>beta+2. Hence dominated convergence proves the full strictly positive finite coefficient for fixed beta,q. Independent SymPy differentiation and four direct positive-real integral evaluations confirmed profile convergence. The derivative/majorant argument, not finite quadrature, proves the infinite limit.

value.rationale: The explicit canonical shear changes from order-two boundary growth at fixed distortion to order-three growth at limiting distortion. The open exponent window is mathematically natural: each finite-parameter weighted moment is finite but the limiting harmonic Koebe moment diverges. An exact two-dimensional profile and leading coefficient quantify the singular crossover, and no whole-class extremality is claimed.

final_claim: For beta>-1 and (beta+2)/3<q<(beta+2)/2, (1-k)^(3q-beta-2) I_{beta,q}(k) tends to the positive finite integral 2^beta/pi int_{x>0,t in R} x^beta |2Re H(x-it)|^q dt dx, H(y)=y^-2-2y^-1+2log(1+1/y); the rescaled harmonic map has local profile 2Re H.
limitations: Only the concrete Koebe shear, fixed beta,q in the strict exponent window, unrooted moment with area factor pi^-1; no endpoint logarithms, uniformity in parameters or whole-class extremal theorem. Some relevant Bergman full texts were not accessible.
